provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Care of the nose and ears
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the rules for nose care.
The pupils should be able to identify clean handkerchiefs.
Introduction:
We use our nose to smell.
We use our ears to hear.
Content:
Do not push things into your nose.
Use a clean handkerchief to blow your nose.
Do not put anything small in your ears.
Ears are delicate.
Class activity:
Show pupils how to blow nose gently into a clean handkerchief.
Evaluation questions:
What do we use to blow our nose?
What should we not put in our ears?
Why do we keep our ears clean?
Summary:
Always take good care of your nose and ears.

topics.title: Care of the hair
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list two ways to care for hair.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate combing hair.
Introduction:
Our hair grows on our head.
We must keep our hair clean.
Content:
Comb my hair every day.
Keep hair clean and short or tied.
Long hair should be tied neatly.
Dirty hair has germs.
Class activity:
Let pupils practice combing doll hair or their own hair with supervision.
Evaluation questions:
How often should we comb our hair?
What happens if we don't wash our hair?
Should we keep long hair loose?
Summary:
Clean and combed hair keeps us healthy.

topics.title: Care of nails
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why nails should be short.
The pupils should be able to show how to wash hands properly.
Introduction:
Nails grow on our fingers.
Dirty nails are not clean.
Content:
Cut nails short every week.
Dirt under nails carries germs.
Wash hands with soap and water.
Clean nails prevent sickness.
Class activity:
Let pupils practice washing hands with soap and water.
Evaluation questions:
What do germs hide under?
How often should we cut our nails?
Why do we wash our hands?
Summary:
Short and clean nails keep us healthy.

topics.title: Germs are not for me
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify germs as tiny and harmful.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate washing hands.
Introduction:
Germs are very small.
Germs make us sick.
Content:
Germs are tiny and make us sick.
Wash germs away with soap.
Do not put dirty hands in mouth.
Germs are everywhere.
Class activity:
Show pupils how to sing while washing hands.
Evaluation questions:
What do germs do to us?
How do we wash germs away?
Where do germs hide?
Summary:
Washing hands keeps germs away.

topics.title: Safe play
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list safe play rules.
The pupils should be able to identify dangerous play areas.
Introduction:\Playing is fun.
We must play safely.
Content:
Play away from the road.
Do not throw sand or stones.
Share toys with friends.
Tell teacher if someone gets hurt.
Class activity:
Let pupils practice safe play movements in the classroom.
Evaluation questions:
Where should we play?
What should we not throw?
What do we do if someone is hurt?
Summary:
Safe play keeps us happy and healthy.

topics.title: Food safety
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state food safety rules.
The pupils should be able to identify clean foods.
Introduction:
Food gives us energy.
We must eat clean food.
Content:
Wash fruits before eating.
Do not pick food from the floor.
Eat food from clean plates.
Dirty food makes us sick.
Class activity:
Let pupils practice washing plastic fruits with water.
Evaluation questions:
What do we do before eating fruits?
Why don't we eat food from the floor?
What makes dirty food bad?
Summary:
Clean food keeps us healthy.

topics.title: Exercise time
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list different exercises.
The pupils should be able to explain why exercise is good.
Introduction:
Exercise makes us strong.
We exercise every day.
Content:
Run, jump and stretch every day.
Exercise makes the body strong.
Exercise helps us grow well.
Exercise keeps us happy.
Class activity:
Lead pupils in simple exercises like jumping and stretching.
Evaluation questions:
What exercise do you like?
Why do we exercise?
How does exercise help us?
Summary:
Exercise keeps our body strong and healthy.

topics.title: Going to the clinic
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state when to go to the clinic.
The pupils should be able to identify the school nurse.
Introduction:
Sometimes we feel sick.
The nurse helps us get well.
Content:
Tell the teacher when I feel sick.
The nurse helps us get well.
The nurse gives medicine.
The nurse is our friend.
Class activity:
Let pupils role play going to the clinic with a doll.
Evaluation questions:
Who helps us when we are sick?
What do we tell the teacher?
What does the nurse do?
Summary:
The nurse helps us stay healthy.

topics.title: Medicine is not sweets
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain that medicine is not for playing.
The pupils should be able to identify who gives medicine.
Introduction:
Medicine helps us get well.
Medicine is not for eating like sweets.
Content:
Never take medicine alone.
Only adults give medicine.
Medicine is not sweets.
Wrong medicine makes us very sick.
Class activity:
Show pupils different medicine bottles and explain they are not toys.
Evaluation questions:
Can we take medicine alone?
Who should give us medicine?
Why is medicine not sweets?
Summary:
Only adults should give us medicine.

topics.title: Revision and health march
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall health habits taught.
The pupils should be able to participate in a health march.
Introduction:
We have learned many health habits.
Let us remember them all.
Content:
Health habits song.
Practise safe play rules.
Wash hands properly.
Keep body clean.
Class activity:
Lead pupils in a health march around the classroom singing health songs.
Evaluation questions:
What did we learn about hair?
How do we keep germs away?
Why is exercise good for us?
Summary:
Health habits keep us strong and happy.
